theorems.name: Two-Asset Markowitz Variance Factorization
theorems.description: Completing-the-square: Var(w) = D·(w - w*)² + V_min where D = σ₁² - 2ρσ₁σ₂ + σ₂², w* is the min-var weight, V_min = σ₁²σ₂²(1-ρ²)/D.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Portfolio.Markowitz

open MathFin

theorem markowitz_variance_factored_thm {σ₁ σ₂ ρ : ℝ}
    (hD : MathFin.minVarDenom σ₁ σ₂ ρ ≠ 0) (w : ℝ) :
    MathFin.portfolioVarTwo σ₁ σ₂ ρ w =
      MathFin.minVarDenom σ₁ σ₂ ρ *
        (w - MathFin.minVarWeightTwo σ₁ σ₂ ρ) ^ 2
      + MathFin.minPortfolioVarTwo σ₁ σ₂ ρ :=
  MathFin.portfolioVarTwo_eq_quad hD w

theorems.description: Beta of a portfolio R_p = w₁R₁ + w₂R₂ is the weighted sum of betas: β_p = w₁β₁ + w₂β₂. Bilinearity of covariance.

    (w₁ w₂ covR₁Rm covR₂Rm : ℝ) :

      w₁ * MathFin.beta covR₁Rm varRm + w₂ * MathFin.beta covR₂Rm varRm :=

theorems.name: N-Asset Markowitz Matches Two-Asset Formula
theorems.description: When the index set has cardinality 2 with weights (w, 1-w) and the standard ρ-parametrized covariance, the n-asset variance recovers the two-asset formula w²σ₁² + (1-w)²σ₂² + 2w(1-w)ρσ₁σ₂.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Portfolio.MarkowitzNAsset

open MathFin

theorem markowitz_n_two_asset_thm (w σ₁ σ₂ ρ : ℝ) :
    MathFin.portfolioVarN (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 2))
        (fun i => if i = 0 then w else 1 - w)
        (fun i j =>
          if i = 0 ∧ j = 0 then σ₁ ^ 2
          else if i = 1 ∧ j = 1 then σ₂ ^ 2
          else ρ * σ₁ * σ₂) =
      w ^ 2 * σ₁ ^ 2 + (1 - w) ^ 2 * σ₂ ^ 2 + 2 * w * (1 - w) * ρ * σ₁ * σ₂ :=
  MathFin.portfolioVarN_two_asset_compat w σ₁ σ₂ ρ

theorems.name: CML Decomposition Uniqueness
theorems.description: Given a target portfolio standard deviation σ_p, the tangent-fund weight on the CML is uniquely α = σ_p/σ_t: that weight attains σ_p (recovery), and any weight attaining σ_p equals it (uniqueness).

code.lean:
import MathFin.Portfolio.TwoFundSeparation

open MathFin

/-- **CML decomposition with unique weight** (two-fund separation): the
    tangent-fund weight `α = σ_p / σ_t` attains the target standard deviation,
    AND any weight attaining it equals `σ_p / σ_t` — existence and uniqueness
    of the decomposition weight. Re-exports
    `MathFin.cml_weight_recovers_stdev` + `MathFin.cml_weight_unique`. -/
theorem cml_decomposition_unique_weight (σ_t σ_p : ℝ) (hσ_t : σ_t ≠ 0) :
    MathFin.cmlStdev σ_t (σ_p / σ_t) = σ_p ∧
    ∀ α, MathFin.cmlStdev σ_t α = σ_p → α = σ_p / σ_t :=
  ⟨MathFin.cml_weight_recovers_stdev σ_t σ_p hσ_t,
   fun α h => MathFin.cml_weight_unique σ_t α σ_p hσ_t h⟩

theorems.name: Omega, Maximum Drawdown, and Calmar

theorem downside_performance_metrics_full
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (m : MathFin.FiniteReturnModel ι) (threshold : ℝ)

    {n : ℕ} (price : Fin n → ℝ) (annualReturn c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) :

theorems.name: Multi-Period Kelly Log-Growth Linearity

open MathFin MeasureTheory

theorem kelly_n_periods_linearity_thm (n : ℕ) {p : ℝ}
    (hp : 0 ≤ p) (hp1 : p ≤ 1) (b f : ℝ) :
    ∫ R : Fin n → ℝ, ∑ i, Real.log (R i)
        ∂(Measure.pi fun _ : Fin n => MathFin.kellyReturnMeasure p b f)
      = (n : ℝ) * MathFin.kellyGrowth p b f :=
  MathFin.kellyGrowth_n_periods n hp hp1 b f

theorems.name: Kelly Numéraire Deflator Makes the Bet Fair (Discrete, Two-Outcome)
theorems.description: In the two-outcome bet (win probability 0 < p < 1, odds b > 0), deflate the physical probabilities by the growth-optimal (Kelly) terminal wealth W*₊ = 1 + f*·b, W*₋ = 1 − f*, where f* = (p·b − (1 − p))/b is the Kelly fraction. The deflated weights q₊ = p/W*₊ and q₋ = (1 − p)/W*₋ give the bet zero expected return: q₊·b + q₋·(−1) = 0. This is the martingale half of the discrete numéraire-portfolio ⟹ EMM identity; the closed forms q₊ = 1/(b+1), q₋ = b/(b+1), their independence of p, and their summing to 1 (which makes q a probability) are not part of this entry's statement.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Performance.KellyNumeraire

open MathFin

/-- **Deflating by the Kelly (growth-optimal) wealth makes the bet fair.** In the
two-outcome market (bet at fraction `f` pays odds `b` with physical
probability `p`), deflate the physical measure by the growth-optimal terminal wealth
`W*₊ = 1 + f*·b`, `W*₋ = 1 - f*` at the Kelly fraction `f* = kellyFraction p b`. The
resulting probabilities `q₊ = p/W*₊`, `q₋ = (1-p)/W*₋` give the bet zero
expected excess return, `q₊·b + q₋·(-1) = 0`: the martingale half of the discrete
numéraire-portfolio ⟹ EMM identity (that `q₊ + q₋ = 1` is not stated here). Re-exports
`MathFin.kellyNumeraire_isRiskNeutral`. -/
theorem kelly_numeraire_isRiskNeutral {p b : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (hb : 0 < b) :
    p / (1 + kellyFraction p b * b) * b
      + (1 - p) / (1 - kellyFraction p b) * (-1) = 0 :=
  MathFin.kellyNumeraire_isRiskNeutral hp hp1 hb

metadata.reference: Numéraire portfolio / benchmark approach (Long 1990; Platen); Kelly growth-optimal criterion
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Re-export of MathFin.kellyNumeraire_isRiskNeutral (MathFin/Performance/KellyNumeraire.lean): the growth-optimal (Kelly) portfolio, used as numéraire, deflates the physical measure into the EMM. Consumes the Kelly fraction kellyFraction and its first-order optimality (kellyGrowth_deriv_at_kelly): 1 + f*·b = p·(b+1), so the GOP-deflated win-probability p/W*₊ = 1/(b+1) is p-independent — the fair-odds risk-neutral probability. HONEST SCOPE: the discrete, two-outcome market — the fully elementary shadow of the continuous Long/Platen benchmark theorem (deflated prices are P-martingales, EMM density ∝ 1/N*), which needs a state-price-density / market model absent from the Itô tower. No axioms beyond Mathlib defaults.
